# Retrospective: PR 12903

## Worked
Fresh Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh sessions received equivalent neutral scope after author and security gates. Both used source-only investigation, avoiding live camera/PipeWire/process access. Waiting for both saved finals kept synthesis independent. Upstream media-class construction resolved a meaningful question without synthetic runtime filler. The public diagram summarizes the exact source path.

## Friction and corrections
The coordinator printed a nested lifecycle object exceeding the 60-line bound. Opus parallelized policy reads despite the aggregate limit, later combined metadata with source output, and truncated a search line before complete re-reading. First-fetch receipt target assertions and status gates were incomplete; one wrong-name decode failed and its empty output was searched. All history is retained, not cleaned away. Corrected dispatch instructions explicitly require sequential chunks, scalar-only metadata, each receipt/decode final target, and expected child status before downstream reads. Both reviewers acknowledged them in closeout.json. No persistent native memory was edited.

The corrected WebRTC source was checked against retained base64 transport by the coordinator, and relevant HTTP/exit receipts were inspected before using it. Public claims are limited to the individually inspected PR and upstream source; no runtime, timing or hardware claim survived by implication. See PROCESS-DEVIATIONS.md for full candid accounting. Process was not fully compliant, though publication is technically supportable under the process-only exception.

## Improvements to carry forward
Use a small scalar-only registry extraction from the first metadata call. Do not use parallel calls for policy reading at all. Fetch helpers should stop on transport failure before any grep and individually guard URL/body/HTTP/stderr/exit/decode paths. Prefer source-only resolution for class/routing errors. Do not promote low-impact code concerns to public findings without concrete relevant impact.

## Tools and resources
No confirmed Herdr, Omadev or review.py bug. No desktop slot or private fixture was used. No reviewer runtime resource remains. Panes, native history, failed decode and all source evidence are preserved. HTML was saved only, never opened. The outer assistant owns publication and the next fresh assignment.
comment:
One camera-detection issue found by source review at `03d1c70`.

### Screen sharing can be reported as camera use

[`camera-busy.sh:5-8`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/03d1c70dc33f4a0a8a8a426c479738a974564806/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/camera-busy.sh#L5-L8) returns `busy` for **any** `Stream/Input/Video` in `pw-dump`, before checking camera devices. That class is not camera-specific: [WebRTC's screencast consumer](https://webrtc.googlesource.com/src/+/refs/heads/main/modules/desktop_capture/linux/wayland/shared_screencast_stream.cc) connects an input-video stream, for which [PipeWire supplies that default class](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire/-/blob/master/src/pipewire/stream.c).

Source-traced path, not a live reproduction:

```text
Non-camera Stream/Input/Video in pw-dump
  -> probe returns busy before checking /dev/video*
  -> Camera.qml sets present=true and inUse=true
  -> record mark and "Camera in use", even without a webcam
```

**Impact:** Screen sharing can produce a misleading camera/privacy indication, including while a connected webcam is idle.

**Suggested change:** Associate the PipeWire consumer with an identified camera source rather than matching the global stream class. Merely finding any `Video/Source` is insufficient, since screen-sharing producers can have that class too. Retain the direct-device check for applications opening `/dev/video*`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source inspection of the pinned widget/probe and upstream PipeWire, WebRTC and portal code. No live webcam, browser screen-share or QML rendering tests. Upstream source snapshots were not matched to installed application versions.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical reviews, then Astra synthesis and source-evidence verification.
